subject: Literature
title: Sinclair Lewis's It Can't Happen Here
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Sinclair Lewis's It Can't Happen Here.

hook.text: In 1935, Sinclair Lewis imagined a fascist dictator winning the American presidency through populist promises.

buildup.text: The novel's demagogue, Buzz Windrip, rises to power by blaming minorities, promising greatness, and attacking the press.

discovery.text: Lewis showed that fascism could come to America not through invasion but through democratic elections and fear.

twist.text: The book resurged in popularity in 2016 and 2020, as readers saw uncomfortable parallels with contemporary politics.

climax.text: The novel's title is its own warning: the phrase 'it can't happen here' is the first step toward it happening.

punchline.text: The most dangerous words in democracy are 'it can't happen here.'

quiz.question: How does fascism come to America in Lewis's novel?
options: Through a military coup by the army
Through democratic elections and populist promises
